elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 gives Customer ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer, but does not cover work product that is not a Deliverable.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Vendor assigns all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable, but there is no assignment of other work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 provides that Vendor retains Vendor Technology, preserving Vendor's existing technology from the Deliverable assignment.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 applies the Section 13.2 perpetual licence to Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable embedded-Vendor-Technology licence irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and transfers no right other than Vendor's limited processing right.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 states that no jointly owned intellectual property is created; any future joint ownership would require a separate signed instrument.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 permits Vendor to retain Vendor Technology, the retained technology category encompassing Vendor's generic tools and know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Customer owns the assigned Deliverable rights, and any retained Vendor Technology incorporated in a Deliverable is subject to Section 13.2's perpetual licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Customer's assigned ownership is not revocable, and Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence to incorporated Vendor Technology irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Customer receives ownership of Deliverables, while Section 13.2 expressly grants worldwide rights in incorporated Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Customer receives assigned ownership, and Section 13.2 makes the licence to incorporated Vendor Technology royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Customer's ownership permits use and modification, and Section 13.2 expressly permits use, modification, and derivative works for Customer's business for incorporated Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 permits contractors only to support incorporated Vendor Technology; it does not grant a general sublicensing right, so Customer cannot necessarily sublicense an entire Deliverable containing that technology.
